critical_code_review_comments: manufacturing_director._decide(): the REJECT-when-blocking branch checks `if verification not in ('Verified',) and not _kr_has_any_content(kr)` — but this branch is only reached when kr is truthy AND _kr_has_any_content(kr) is true (checked earlier), so the second half of the AND is always False and the branch is dead code. HOLD is always returned when blocking/missing exists on a KR with content, regardless of verification. Consider removing the dead branch or clarifying intent (e.g., REJECT if unverified AND all sections empty for the requested products).

manufacturing_director.review_queue(): iterates every order and calls review_order() serially (N+1 db lookups per order: _find_kr scans all KRs + inspect_kr_for_manufacture). With 20 orders this is fine (~200ms observed), but at 500 orders the queue will be slow. Consider caching KR list once per queue call and batching, or building a fast summary variant of review_order().

routers/director.py apply_decision: no idempotency guard. Re-applying to the same order re-appends a duplicate approval_history entry every call; consider skipping the update if order.status == new_status AND last history entry is already the Director's identical verdict.

manufacturing_director._find_kr: `overlap = len(topic_words & tw) / len(tw)` uses KR-title word count as denominator. Short titles (e.g., 2 words) can spuriously match if 1 word overlaps (0.5 threshold). Consider using min(len(tw), len(topic_words)) or Jaccard for stability.

ManufacturingDirector.js ReviewPanel.load: on failure `setR(false)` and the UI shows 'Could not load the review.' — but there is no retry button; user must close+reopen. Add a retry action for resilience.

ManufacturingDirector.js: clicking director-apply-decision has no confirmation dialog. Because applying mutates order status (moves to Research or Queued), a confirm modal (or an 'Undo in 5s' toast) would prevent accidental state changes on the queue.

ManufacturingDirector.js: filter 'held' merges HOLD+REJECT which is fine for the summary metric intent, but the button label is 'Held' — consider 'Held / Rejected' or a 4-state filter (All | Cleared | Held | Rejected) to align with the four verdicts shown in MetricCards.
